parole.significato: a cable (conductor – heavily insulated wire, fiber-optic cable, network cable, etc. – same as in English)
parole.testo: From Old Swedish kabel (“heavy rope”), kabbla (plural) (15th c.), from Old Norse kabill (14th c.), by some merit a derivative of kabb- (“spool, roll”) + -ill (agent suffix), related to kafli (“roll; handle, swordhilt”), but also a derivative of Old Northern French cable, Occitan câble, from Late Lat

From Old Swedish kær, from Old Norse kærr, from Old Northern French ker, kier, quer (Old French chier, cher), from Latin cārus (“dear”), from Proto-Italic *kāros, from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂- (“to desire, to wish”). Doublet of hora.
